article.headline: Shared Memory Between AI Agents, Built on Flat Files
article.lede: A developer's demo of two AI agents collaborating on code in Slack — then recalling that work verbatim on Telegram — drew attention in the multi-agent community. The project, icarus-daedalus, is the work of an anonymous developer known as esaradev and runs as a plugin for NousResearch's Hermes Agent framework. The mechanism is simpler than the framing suggests, and more carefully engineered than the marketing implies.
article.body:
The demo is genuine. Two agents — Icarus and Daedalus — collaborated on a WebSocket pub/sub broker in Node.js, critiqued each other's code, then, when Icarus was queried on Telegram, it reconstructed the full session: the incomplete methods, Daedalus's critique, the rewrite. The trick is not a memory protocol. It is a shared directory. Both agents point their IcarusMemory instances at the same local filesystem path. What one writes from any platform, the other reads at session start.

The library doing the real work is **icarus-memory-infra**, seventeen Python modules. Each memory entry is a markdown file with YAML frontmatter — a metadata block at the top of the file — recording the agent name, the platform it ran on, a summary, the full body, and crucially a verification status and lifecycle state (active or superseded). Older facts are never overwritten; they are marked superseded and linked to their replacements, creating an audit trail the library calls a *supersession chain*. Before each task, a briefing compiler reads a shared wiki and the agent's own archive, explicitly surfacing failed prior attempts so agents do not repeat dead ends.

The project lives in the ecosystem of **Hermes Agent**, an open-source autonomous-agent framework NousResearch launched in February 2026. Hermes Agent supports multi-platform deployment — Slack, Telegram, Discord, WhatsApp — and ships a community plugin directory called Hermes Atlas. Teknium, NousResearch's co-founder and primary author of the Hermes model series, flagged the plugin on X, which drove much of its early visibility. icarus-daedalus is a third-party community contribution, not an official NousResearch product.

The tweet cites an arxiv paper calling cross-platform persistent memory “the most pressing open challenge” in multi-agent systems. The paper — arXiv:2603.10062, “Multi-Agent Memory from a Computer Architecture Perspective,” by Zhongming Yu and colleagues — is real. It frames multi-agent memory as a *cache coherence* problem, borrowing from classical computer-architecture theory, and identifies *multi-agent memory consistency* as the field's most urgent unsolved challenge. The paper does not address Slack-to-Telegram recall specifically; the tweet's citation is a reasonable but loose interpretation of a more abstract architectural argument.

The “no infrastructure” framing holds for the minimal path: keyword search over flat files needs no server, no model, no database. An optional embeddings layer adds a local model and *hybrid BM25 retrieval*, which is infrastructure of a quieter kind. The project is six weeks old, holds 272 stars on GitHub, and its developer has no verifiable prior public footprint. The design is credible; the scope is modest.

concepts.definition: A linked sequence of memory entries tracking how a fact evolves over time. When an entry is updated or contradicted, the old version is marked 'superseded' and linked to its replacement rather than deleted. The full revision history is preserved, enabling rollback to any earlier verified state.

A block of structured metadata written in YAML (a human-readable serialization format) at the top of a markdown file, enclosed in triple-dash delimiters. Used in icarus-memory-infra to attach fields like agent name, platform, timestamp, and verification status to each memory entry stored as a flat file.

The challenge of keeping a shared body of knowledge synchronized across multiple AI agents running independently. When two agents update the same fact separately, their representations can diverge; resolving that divergence without data loss is the core problem, analogous to cache coherence in computer architecture.

In computer architecture, the guarantee that all processors in a multi-core system observe the same value for a shared memory location at any given time. Researchers have borrowed the concept for multi-agent AI: when two agents hold conflicting versions of the same fact, a coherence protocol must decide which is authoritative.

A search strategy combining BM25 — a keyword-ranking algorithm scoring documents by term frequency and length — with cosine-similarity scores from a neural embedding model. Results from both methods are merged using Reciprocal Rank Fusion, producing rankings that capture both exact-keyword matches and semantic proximity.

A community-maintained plugin directory for NousResearch's Hermes Agent framework, listing open-source extensions built by third-party developers. Plugins can add new memory providers, tools, or platform integrations to any Hermes Agent deployment without modifying the core framework.

An open-source autonomous-agent framework released by NousResearch in February 2026, distinct from the Hermes LLM model series. It supports multi-platform deployment across Slack, Telegram, Discord, WhatsApp, and others, any LLM backend, and a pluggable memory and skills system. Community plugins are distributed via Hermes Atlas.

repos.summary: Reference demo showing two Hermes Agent instances (Icarus and Daedalus) sharing persistent memory across platforms using icarus-memory-infra. The setup wires the library into a minimal two-agent collaboration loop with session logging. Useful as a starting point for understanding how the memory library integrates with the Hermes Agent plugin system.

The installable Hermes Agent plugin packaging icarus-memory-infra as a drop-in memory provider, listed in Hermes Atlas. Adds structured markdown memory, briefing compilation, supersession chains, and optional hybrid retrieval to any Hermes Agent deployment without modifying the core framework.

article.fact_check: The tweet's arxiv citation is accurate but reframes the paper's finding. arXiv:2603.10062 identifies 'multi-agent memory consistency' as the most pressing open challenge — not 'cross-platform persistent memory' specifically; the two are related but not synonymous. The 'no infrastructure' claim accurately describes the default keyword-search path but elides the optional local-embedding layer (BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5), which does require a local model. The 'two weeks ago' timing is consistent with a tweet sent in late March 2026, when the March 9 paper submission would have been approximately two weeks old.
